# `unresolved-member`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: semantic · Profile: none · Default: error · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a field, declaration, or method access that is absent from a receiver
whose complete shape is known: a local container, or an imported module whose
public members the host resolved.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Renaming a container member should identify every stale qualified use
immediately instead of waiting for a later compiler pass.

## When it fires

The rule checks locally declared structs, enums, and tagged unions, plus
bindings declared with one: by a type path such as `Inner` or `Outer.Inner`
(resolved where it is written, segment by segment), a struct literal, or a call
to a function declared to return it. It stays silent for incomplete compiler
shapes, containers extended with `usingnamespace`, error sets merged with `||`,
and members the file tests for with `@hasDecl` or `@hasField`, since such an
access may sit in a branch comptime never analyzes.

It also checks `alias.name` where `alias` is a top-level constant bound to an
imported file or to a container inside one (`const m = @import("m.zig");`,
`const Inner = @import("m.zig").Outer.Inner;`) and `name` is not a public
declaration there. The language server and `zig-analyzer check` both resolve
the imported files; an import that cannot be read or followed is not judged,
nor is an empty file (Zig's release archives empty the standard library's test
files) or a type function with more than one `return`, whose result depends on
its comptime arguments.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Point = struct { x: i32, y: i32 };

pub fn main() void {
    const p: Point = .{ .x = 1, .y = 2 };
    _ = p.z;
}
```
